      • 20,000 Pa Robot Vacuum for Deep Cleaning: Power through dust, pet hair, crumbs, and debris with 20,000 Pa HyperForce suction. This robot vacuum and mop automatically boosts suction on carpets while delivering powerful cleaning across hardwood, tile, and other hard floors
      • Zero-Tangle Cleaning for Pet-Friendly Homes: The Dual Zero-Tangle System combines an anti-tangle side brush with the DuoDivide main brush to minimize hair wrap while effectively lifting long hair and pet fur. Spend less time maintaining your robot vacuum cleaner and more time enjoying clean floors
      • FlexiArm Tech Cleans Every Edge & Corner: The FlexiArm Edge Mopping System extends to clean as close as 1.85 mm along walls for exceptional edge coverage, while the reversible side brush reaches deep into corners for up to 30% more corner coverage. Capture dust where traditional robot vacuums often miss
      • Carpet Care Protects Every Floor: Designed for mixed-floor homes, this robot vacuum automatically removes the mop when needed, vacuums carpets before mopping, lifts the mopping module up to 15 mm, and boosts suction for deeper carpet cleaning. Transition seamlessly between hardwood, tile, rugs, and low-pile carpets without extra effort
      • Self-Emptying Dock Cleans & Dries Automatically: The upgraded multifunctional dock automatically empties dust, refills the water tank, performs 65°C high-temperature mop self-cleaning, dries the mop with 45°C warm air, and features a upgraded cleaning tray with soaking mode for easier upkeep
      • Smart Navigation Avoids Everyday Obstacles: Reactive Tech Obstacle Avoidance helps the robot vacuum move smoothly around everyday obstacles. Quick Mapping rapidly creates your home layout, while 3D Map Display lets you customize cleaning with greater accuracy and control
      • Smart Cleaning That Adapts to Your Home: Roborock SmartPlan 3.0 automatically adjusts cleaning based on your home, floor types, and cleaning history. Operating at a quiet 54 dB, this robot vacuum is ideal for homes with children and pets, delivering powerful cleaning with less disruption
      See more

        The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro ROCKS! Why did I wait so long to buy this?

        Reviewed in Canada on October 8, 2026
        Colour Name: Black
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
        Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

        I honestly don’t know why I waited so long to upgrade my robot vacuum. I had an older iRobot for over 10 years, so I knew what a robot vacuum could do, but the Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is on a completely different level. I’ve only had it a short time, and I’m already a little obsessed with this machine!

        My house has hardwood floors, tile, area rugs and carpet, so I needed something that could handle different surfaces. I also have a fluffy cat, and between her fur, my own long hair, everyday dust and all the little bits of debris that somehow appear on the floor every day, keeping the floors clean feels like a never-ending job. I wanted something that would actually help take that job off my hands, rather than just give me another gadget to manage.

        So far, this little machine is delivering! The vacuuming is impressive. It picks up hair, dust and all those little bits of dirt you don’t necessarily realize are there until you see what it collects. There is something ridiculously satisfying about watching it clean and knowing I don’t have to drag out the vacuum myself. I’m especially interested to see how much cat hair it collects over time, because there is certainly no shortage of that in my house!

        But the mopping is where this machine really won me over. First of all, can we talk about the little mop pads?! They look like tiny pantaloons, and I absolutely love them. 😂 And when the robot kicks its little “leg” out to mop along an edge, I cannot get over how adorable it is. Who knew a robot vacuum could have so much personality? I find myself watching it work far more than I probably should. It’s ridiculously entertaining for something that is supposed to be doing chores!

        Beyond being cute, the mopping system is genuinely clever. The robot vacuums and mops, then returns to its dock to wash its own mop pads, refill its water and continue cleaning when needed. When the job is finished, the dock can wash and dry the pads, too. I love that I don’t have to remove the mop pads and wash them myself after every run or constantly stop what I’m doing to tend to the machine.

        The dock is a big part of what makes this system so appealing. It handles so much of the maintenance automatically, which is exactly what I wanted. Yes, the dock takes up some space, but for the convenience it provides, I think it’s well worth it.

        Now, I will say that there is a learning curve. This is not a machine you take out of the box, press one button on, and immediately have everything perfectly set up. It takes time to get to know the machine, learn your way around the app, map out your rooms and customize everything to suit your home.

        Getting the maps right takes some patience, especially if you want to make adjustments, get the rooms organized properly and manually add obstacles or no-go areas so the robot knows where you don’t want it to go. That part can be time-consuming. You need to spend a little time figuring out how you want it to navigate your home and learning where all the settings are in the app.

        At first, there is quite a bit to learn, and you may find yourself going back into the app to change things or fine-tune your maps. But honestly? I think the time spent getting everything set up properly is absolutely worth it. Once you understand how the app works and have your rooms and obstacles mapped the way you want them, you have much more control over how the machine cleans. You can customize the settings to suit your own home instead of having to work around a one-size-fits-all cleaning routine.

        I actually like being able to fine-tune things. I’ve already adjusted the frequency at which it returns to wash its mop pads, setting it to every 20 minutes. I like knowing I can change that depending on how dirty the floors are and what areas I’m cleaning. I’m still learning all the features, but that’s part of the fun of owning it.

        The mapping and app setup are probably the biggest things I would tell a new buyer to be prepared for. Give yourself time, play around with the settings, and don’t expect to have everything figured out on day one. It’s worth putting in the effort rather than rushing through the setup and missing out on the features that make this machine so useful.

        I also love the convenience of having the robot take care of so much on its own. I can let it clean while I get on with my day, and it takes care of washing its mop pads, managing its water and drying the pads when it’s finished. It feels much closer to having a little cleaning helper than simply owning another vacuum.

        I did spend time comparing models before buying because these machines are an investment, and I wanted something that would work for my particular home. Between the mix of flooring, the pet hair and the desire to have both vacuuming and mopping handled with as little manual work as possible, the Qrevo 2 Pro seemed like the right choice. So far, I’m very happy with that decision.

        I’m still in the early days of owning it, so I can’t comment on long-term reliability just yet. But my first impressions are excellent. I love watching it work, I love seeing what it picks up, and I love that I’m spending less time thinking about vacuuming and mopping.

        And yes, I am absolutely entertained by those tiny pantaloons and the little leg that pops out to mop. It’s the little things!

        My advice to anyone considering this machine: do your research, take the time to set it up properly, learn the app, and be patient while you map your home and adjust the settings. There is a bit of a learning curve, but once you start getting everything dialled in, you can really appreciate what it can do.

        If you have pets, a mixture of flooring, lots of hair and dust, or simply want to spend less time doing floors, I would definitely recommend putting the Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro on your shortlist.

        I went from an old robot vacuum that had served me well for over a decade to this clever little machine, and the difference is remarkable.

        Premium robot cleaner that will take a bit of study to get maximum benefit.

        Reviewed in Canada on September 11, 2026
        Colour Name: Black
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.

        This robot vacuum is awesome. It does the stuff you expect: map the floor plan, vacuum the floor, don't cause damage. This is my second robot vacuum and it is superior to the other for obstacle avoidance and adapting to surface changes. It does not get caught on the area carpet and anti-fatigue mats don't bother it either. Occasionally, a shoelace will get caught in the roller brush and that is easy to untangle. The mop feature is something special. The robot will use rotating pads and cleaning solution (or plain water) to mop the floor. Dirty rinse water is collected by the base station for dumping when it gets full. My only hesitation to award 5 stars relates to the hickups I experienced with network connectivity. For some reason my home router dislikes the traffic produced by the robot. When the ap on my smartphone reports a network outage I turn off the wifi and use my cellular data to connect with the roborock service. The robot will map the floor and vaccuum manually if you are not connected with the ap. However, you need the ap and connectivity to update the floor plan, specify rooms, no-go areas and instructions about mopping. To get the full benefit of this device you will probably need to spend some time learning about the features and how they apply to your dwelling. I do like the way the base station is designed and how the robot is sheltered in it when docked. This is a premium product.

        This thing is such an upgrade! My floors have never been cleaner.

        Reviewed in the United States on September 3, 2026
        Colour Name: White-02
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
        Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

        I had a very (very-very) basic robot vacuum that I was happy enough with, so I was sad when it finally went kaput. I definitely wanted to replace it. After much research and deliberation--and feeling completely overwhelmed at the vast number of choices--I finally settled on the Roborock Qrevo S5V and I am so happy with my choice. I am so impressed with how well it functions and all the things it does to make my life easier and my house cleaner! It is controlled mainly with the Roborock app, and if there is something you want done, the app will pretty much let you tell the robot to do it. You can vacuum only, mop only, vacuum the whole house then mop the whole house, or set it to sort of vacuum and mop at the same time (though not actually at the very same time). You can tell it what time to start working on what day, and make your schedule as complicated or as simplified as you like. One huge feature for me is that while my old robot just kind of wandered around randomly, the Qrevo S5V methodically covers every square inch. I can look at the app and see exactly where it has cleaned and where it has not. this feature is excellent and such a huge upgrade.

        As far as how well it cleans, I am so impressed with the vacuuming, especially. I have long hair, two dogs and lots of nature outside, so my own hair, dog hair, leaves, grass clippings and dust seem to build up on my floors very quickly. The S5V's brushes and suctioning do a thorough job of picking it all up, but I do find I need to manually clean corners and some other oddly shaped spaces the robot can't get to. I really love the split roller brushes ("DuoDivide" brushes) because they prevent dog hair (and my own long hair) from tangling and gumming up the brushes. I am not quite sure how it works, but it is a marvel of engineering that after vacuuming, the two roller brushes are nearly hair free and tangles are not an issue. It is because of the split design. If you have pets or long hair of your own, whether you get the S5V or some other Roborock model, I recommend making sure it has the DuoDivide brush feature.

        As for mopping, this feature is really helping me out because my home has lots of square feet of polished concrete, and mopping the whole thing is quite the dreaded chore. The robot's mopping job is not as thorough as a manual one done by a human, but between the vacuum's regularly scheduled dust/hair removal followed by the basic mopping job, this robot is keeping my floors cleaner and looking so much better than they have in years. Mopping the floors in this house is such a chore that I would have to psyche myself up for the job, but now that this robot takes care of so much of it for me, the floors look nice day-in/day-out, and when I want to give them a thorough mopping myself, it's so much quicker and easier because the floors are soooo much cleaner to start with. Even if I have skipped my own mopping job, I am not embarrassed if friends or neighbors drop by unannounced because my floors look nice at all times thanks to this robot.

        I do get tripped up on the app sometimes when programming jobs, but there is a wonderful Roborock community on Reddit and all I have to do it post a question there and someone helpful will answer it. Overall, I am extrememly pleased with the Qrevo S5V. My floors have never looked better and with so little effort. It has inspired me to keep my entire house cleaner and also given me more time to attend to other areas of my home.

      • RodeHaus
        4 out of 5 stars
        Verified Purchase

        Roborock QRevo 2 Pro - better than narwal and Roomba

        Reviewed in the United States on September 21, 2026
        Colour Name: Black
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
        Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

        I've been through a bunch of these types of robots recently due to various design issues. So, take my review as a matter of perspective versus other robots like it.

        I had originally been avoiding the roborock brand because I had owned two of them before; way back before they adopted the roborock name, they still went by their Chinese name. I got really turned off by them because they had no support for American customers, then as they started rolling out Roborock branded vacuums, they just didn't care about any models prior and stopped supporting me. After having so much problems with other brands I got on the dedicated Reddit thread and found out that roborock has absolutely stepped up its game. They are now the gold standard for reliability and customer support in vacuum + mopping robots. So I'm telling you look no further than the roborock brand but you need to make sure to get the model that suits your needs, don't assume this model is the best, it's what works for me with all tile, plus area rugs.

        I owned two different Narwals:

        - Freo Z10 Ultra - good but the dock got all gummed up after 1.5 years of use. This is because I use tap water without detergent, so it got scale and mold. I didn't have warranty tried to DIY the fix. It was a nightmare. Wasn't designed modularly, so it gave up after matters got worse. $1k down the drain.

        - Freo ZT10 Turbo - I gave narwal another try because I chalked it up to my own poor decision to use tap water and no detergent, but it was a disaster. Design issues with the dock and removable washing tray. Always leaking water, had to convince AMZ to allow me to return after ~45 days because Narwal didn't support me, so no more Narwals for me...DONE. The email conversations were SO frustrating with their offers for free accessories that didn't fix the design issue.

        Then I tried Roomba 575 because I thought an "American" brand would support me better. I found issues with the thing right away and never got a response to my support tickets, so returned it within 30 days. The deal breaker was it wouldn't stay connected to WiFi. Cheep, old WiFi hardware wasn't compatible with my modern WiFi router; and trust me I tried some really advanced configuration on my router to dedicate a bare bones 2.5ghz-only SSID to it; no dice. I did some better research after the fact and found out that the iRobot company is going through some serious financial struggles and they're just not worth dealing with anymore. They're basically Chinese owned at this point anyways and can't keep up with competition. I highly advise everyone to stay away from Roomba at this point. Dying brand.

        So onto this robot... what's better:

        - The Wi-Fi in the app just work. Zero set up issues. The mapping software is easy to use and name all my runes then connect it to Google (or whatever smart home) to get it to clean rooms on demand with just voice. Awesome. Routines and scheduling is easy to set up as well.

        - The new roller brush design is BADA$$. It really doesn't tangle. I'm actually blown away. It does have both rubber and bristles so that it works fairly well on low pile rugs, but the magic is that the brush is split in two at the middle, which allows the tangling hair to pull towards the middle and get sucked up into the vacuum at the gap. It's brilliant.

        - it navigates and avoids obstacles like a pro. I'd say my original narwal was about as good at navigation but all the others were terrible compared to this.

        - The "FlexiArm" works well. My Roomba and second narwal had this as well, all about equal, but I thought it was worth noting no issues so far. It gets in the corners and up against the baseboards.

        - it's got a really cool feature where it leaves the mop pads behind when you do "carpet first" or vacuum only. This wasn't a huge deal to me, but it avoided an issue I had with other robots where the mop pads would get lodged up under my rugs and pulled off, so I'd have to go fix it...if I was around. Since the mop heads aren't involved at all in vacuuming my rugs, that issue just doesn't happen. Again, brilliant.

        - battery life is awesome. I have ~1,700 square feet downstairs (of mostly tile) that this thing covers and it has never run out of battery mid-cycle in the middle of a cleaning unless I put it on deep clean for the entire downstairs.

        - it has a little onboard tank that keeps the mop wet as it's cleaning without going back to the dock. That's much more efficient. The narwals didn't have this, so they were constantly going back to the dock, which may sound like it's going to get things cleaner but it's just inefficient.

        What I don't like, or things that you might want to just be aware of:

        - no dedicated detergent tank/dispenser. This by biggest one...really the only reason not 5 stars. My other vacuums all had the ability to just snap in a bottle of detergent and it would automatically mix into the cleaning water. Roborock dock doesn't have that feature at all, and they don't give you any with the robot. They sell specialized detergent for these but they don't even mention that using RO or distilled water with detergent will absolutely keep your dock from gumming up like my narwal did. If you don't use ro/ distilled water, you'll get scale, and if you don't use detergent, you'll get mold. So, with this roborock, I will absolutely be manually mixing their specialized detergent into RO water. DO NOT USE ANY OTHER DETERGENT. That is kind of a pain though because you have to measure based on how much you are topping off or let it run dry every time.

        - Just FYi, what I said earlier about not going back to the dock to re-wet the mops constantly means it is not mopping with hot water most of the time, or at all really. So the advertisement about using 170° water is just about what cleans the mop with at the dock. Not what it is cleaning the floor with. I think that is fine, the mop heads aren't going to stay at 170° very long anyways, but be aware that's what you're getting. This makes it extra important to use the detergent that they barely even acknowledge you should be using.

        - Roborock app does not allow you to create named zones to reuse. All the other makers did, and this is useful because you can then schedule a zone such as a carpet, with specific vacuuming settings like going over it meticulously multiple times, and make that a routine/automation. This is really a shame because when I put a zone over my living room carpet and tell it to do it meticulously multiple times at maximum strength it actually gets the majority of the dog hair. However, there is no way for me to do this on a scheduled basis unless I tell it to clean my entire living room under such parameters. The rest of my living room doesn't need that kind of meticulousness because it's just tile. If this was a named zone, I could schedule that activity of just my carpet or do a voice command to do it when I notice a little dog hair building up on the carpet. That would be bliss for me, but now I have to do it in the app which is about a 2-minute process each time.

        - as noted above, when I have this robot go over my living room rug coated in dog hair multiple times meticulously it gets most of the hair but otherwise it does not with just normal "carpet boost". The same "carpet boost" feature on my narwals actually got the majority of the hair. Don't get me wrong, I still manually vacuum my living room rug every 1 or 2 weeks, but I would love it to look better in the meantime without the manual steps I described earlier.

      Product description

      The Roborock 2026 New Qrevo 2 Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop combines 20,000Pa HyperForce suction for deep cleaning of dust, pet hair, crumbs, and debris across hardwood, tile, and carpets, automatically boosting suction on carpets. Its Dual Zero-Tangle System features an anti-tangle side brush and DuoDivide main brush to minimize hair wrap, reducing maintenance. The FlexiArm Edge Mopping System extends to 1.85mm along walls for exceptional coverage, while the reversible side brush reaches corners for up to 30% more coverage. Designed for mixed floors, it automatically removes the mop, vacuums carpets before mopping, lifts the module 15mm, and boosts suction for carpets. The upgraded dock empties dust, refills water, self-cleans the mop at 149°F, dries with 113°F warm air, and features a soaking mode tray. Reactive Tech Obstacle Avoidance ensures smooth navigation, Quick Mapping creates layouts, and 3D Map Display enables customization. SmartPlan 3.0 adapts to your home’s layout, floor types, and history, operating at 54dB for quiet, child- and pet-friendly cleaning.
